subject: PrivNet: post-call checklist & next steps for BrightBank private connectivity
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Rivers <jordan.rivers@brightbank.com>, Priya Sinha <priya.sinha@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-03-25T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: PrivNet: post-call checklist & next steps for BrightBank private connectivity

Thanks again for your time earlier, Jordan and Priya — helpful call. Quick recap + the minimal set of next actions so we can scope Dedicated vs Private VPC (and decide whether PrivateLink or VPC peering is the right path).

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary requirement: tenant isolation + bank-internal audit logs (S3 export) and customer-managed KMS.
- Latency target: 50ms median for in-region requests; bursty daytime traffic on weekdays.
- Preferred hosting: BrightBank legal prefers Private VPC, but engineering is open to Dedicated if networking/egress overhead is too high.

Immediate asks / owner
1) Please confirm the BrightBank networking contact (name + email) who can provide: VPC CIDR ranges, firewall egress rules, and whether you can create a PrivateLink endpoint in your VPC. (action: Jordan)
2) Share the minimal list of IP ranges you will allowlist for outbound egress from Redwood (we can provide our NAT pool and NAT rotation cadence). If you prefer PrivateLink, allowlist will be smaller. (action: Priya)
3) We attached a quick topology sketch and a template spreadsheet for requirements. Fill the sheet with expected peak RPS per environment (prod/staging) and any static IP ranges. (action: BrightBank ops)

Marissa, Kimberly — can you take point on a quick feasibility check for:
- If BrightBank wants PrivateLink, what our onboarding steps and lead times look like?
- If they go with VPC peering, what IP ownership and route table changes do we expect?

Next upstream items from our side
- I'll schedule a 30-min technical sync between BrightBank netops and our infra team this week.
- I'll follow up with a HubSpot link to capture the SOW checklist and a DocuSign for a standard data processing addendum if needed.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0198
redwoodinference.com

Ben — thanks, that matches our notes. Quick answers inline: 

1) Networking contact: Marcus Holt (marcus.holt@brightbank.com). He owns peering and endpoint work. I'll loop him when we set the technical sync.
2) For allowlist: as of now our security team prefers to lock to specific provider egress IPs rather than broad ranges. We can start with a flat list of three /24s if you can provide them. PrivateLink would be preferred to avoid egress flow logging complexities.
3) Peak RPS: Prod ~200 rps sustained during daytime; peak bursts to 1k rps for occasional batch processing windows. Staging is ~2 rps.

We also require that any S3 export to our audit bucket use our KMS key and include server-side encryption. Happy to share IAM role ARNs once we get closer.

Jordan
Director, Infrastructure Engineering
BrightBank

Subject: Re: PrivNet: post-call checklist & next steps for BrightBank private connectivity

Looping in a quick technical note from infra:

PrivateLink path (recommended if BrightBank security prefers provider endpoint model)
- Pros: no public egress for traffic, smaller allowlist (only interface endpoint IPs), simpler compliance for audit logs.
- Cons: requires you to create/approve an interface endpoint and share subnet IDs; additional per-endpoint constructs for each region/env.
- Onboarding: estimate 2-3 business days once subnets and an IAM contact are provided; we will need the VPC ID, 1-2 subnets for endpoint ENIs, and route table confirmation.

VPC peering path
- Pros: straightforward routing, predictable IP paths.
- Cons: requires route table changes and potential CIDR overlap checks; egress for logging still crosses peering unless we establish a proxy/NAT.
- Onboarding: estimate 3-7 business days depending on NetOps windows and whether they require change approvals.

IP allowlist: we can provide a current NAT pool of 3 /24s and rotate them monthly. If you confirm PrivateLink, allowlist needs only the endpoint's ENI addresses (smaller set).

Next steps I suggest (concrete)
- Jordan: loop Marcus Holt into this thread and share preferred time windows for a 30-min sync.
- Priya: please populate the attached spreadsheet with the RPS numbers and a primary NetOps contact.
- Ben: please send the HubSpot checklist + DPA link so procurement can start internal approvals.

I'll prepare a short runbook we can share with BrightBank NetOps showing the exact request payloads (endpoint creation, peering request) and required firewall ports.

Thanks — Marissa

--
